properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live SHA-1 in two deliberate places in this RSA/EC key-weakness detector: (1) keypair_generator.py:38-41 re-implements the npm "keypair" package's broken PRNG (CVE-2021-41117) — SHA-1 chained seed→t→key→seed derives the AES key/seed used to generate test RSA keypairs the CheckKeypair detector must flag; the module header explicitly warns the implementation is deliberately vulnerable and must not be copied. (2) rsa_single_checks.py:205 (CheckOpensslDenylist) computes a SHA-1 hexdigest suffix of t

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is a first-class curve in ec_util.py's CURVE_FACTORY (lines 1043-1044, full domain parameters), consumed live by the check engine (ec_single_checks.py:47,78, ecdsa_sig_checks.py:86,244, hidden_number_problem.py:401 via CURVE_FACTORY.get/[]) so the detector can validate EC public keys and detect biased ECDSA nonces on the Bitcoin curve. Remaining sites are test fixtures (good/bad EC keys and ECDSA signatures in *_test.py) and per-curve truncated-LCG constants in lcg_constants.py feeding

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Python random (Mersenne Twister) in a randomness-detection library: rng.py:108-109 is the deliberate test-subject wrapper Mt19937 for the statistical test suite — weak RNGs are the library's subject matter, and the docstring documents that FindBias/linear-complexity tests must detect it. All other sites are unit tests generating arbitrary scalars, EC points, roots and primes (e.g. gmpy.next_prime(random.getrandbits(1024)) for Fermat-factorization test data). Never used to protect a secret. Relat

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp384r1, secp521r1 and brainpoolP384r1 (grouped here by bit size) are live entries in ec_util.py's CURVE_FACTORY (963-964, 1011-1012, 1089-1090), consumed by the EC/ECDSA check engine for point validation and nonce-bias detection. Other sites: U2F/CR50 ECDSA sample (cr50_u2f_weakness_test.py), GMP truncated-LCG per-curve constants in lcg_constants.py and EcdsaSample fixtures for the hidden-number-problem detector (hidden_number_problem_test.py), and good-key/signature fixtures in paranoid_ec_t

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shake128 class in the randomness test suite wraps hashlib.shake_128 (rng.py:79) as the known-good CSPRNG baseline: the docstring states all statistical tests must pass with it, otherwise the test is buggy. Registered in the RNG name→instance table at rng.py:616 and exercised with fixed seeds in rng_test.py:27,30. FIPS 202 XOF; not Shor-relevant (Grover only halves output security) — quantum rating A-. First-party, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: os.urandom (OS CSPRNG) is the library's secure randomness source: the Urandom wrapper class, default seeding of the test-subject RNG wrappers (truncated LCG, xorshift, JavaRandom, Lehmer, MWC, subset-sum states), SHAKE-128 unseeded path, and Berlekamp-Massey/matrix-rank test inputs. Correct choice everywhere randomness need not be reproducible; quantum rating '?' only because a DRBG is not Shor-relevant. First-party, changeable here.
